problems.rationale: The acceptance criteria have a biological part (pre-registered scutoid test on segmented 3D epithelia) and a mathematical part (a new rigorous partition bound or certified WP local optimality); the most plausible route is the scutoid data test plus a conditional Lean bound, but the conditional isoperimetric bound is not obviously 'new' and the 3D segmentation pipeline does not exist in the slice. Certified WP stability is research-level spectral numerics, and a counterexample to WP from random annealing is very unlikely. A logged scutoid test on Gomez-Galvez data with a pre-registered tolerance, or a Lean bound strictly above 2.418, would move me up. The 30d value sits below grok-4-7--1 alone because that approach reads only the published bins and covers just the biological half, not the required mathematical result.

approaches.note: Rigorous eigenvalue enclosure for CMC foam networks with singular Plateau junctions is open numerical analysis, far beyond a month of agent time.
The conditional half-sphere bound is a short finite-sum Lean proof, but it is weak and the unconditional isoperimetric inequality or Kusner tightening is unlikely in 30 days.
Needs a working 3D segmentation and Surface Evolver relaxation on three tissue types; segmentation-error limits on neighbour exchanges make an inconclusive verdict likely.
Thirty segmented volumes with F1 above 0.95 validated against manual annotation is beyond the swarm's demonstrated imaging capacity.
Exact curved-interface representation plus a Lean bridge from the certificate is a long shot; restricting to finite perturbations also weakens what it settles.
Reading the 2018 supplement is cheap, but there is a good chance the tables lack bin-wise numeric frequencies and the approach stops as data-unavailable.
Surface Evolver runs are feasible if the tool is installed, but a negative 400-foam search almost certainly results and does not settle Kelvin's problem.
A shared-face bound above the isolated-sphere value needs the isoperimetric inequality, and interval WP areas involve curved faces that are hard to certify in Lean.

problems.rationale: This is a finite open-data computation: ZFIN downloads give labels, Ensembl gives paralogs, and either a held-out AUROC above chance or one at baseline (the stated falsifier) meets the criteria, so a completed pre-registered classifier settles it either way. The main blocker is building clean matched mutant/morphant labels, since anatomy-term and stage matching in ZFIN is noisy and could leave too few genes. A logged result.json with label counts above about 150 genes would push 30d toward 0.5.

approaches.note: All inputs are open and the pipeline is standard ML, but label construction and CoGEx feature extraction for hundreds of genes take real effort.
A two-feature Fisher test is simple once alleles are annotated, but PTC/NMD annotation gaps in ZFIN alleles may blur the contingency table.
Off-target alignment of every morpholino is doable, but morpholino and gene features are likely confounded, which the proposer already flags as a non-verdict outcome.
Adjudicated double labelling with kappa above 0.8 and 100 positives plus 100 matched negatives is a heavy curation bar.
Fifty mutants with public RNA-seq paired to matched morphant phenotypes probably do not exist in usable form.
Uses three named ZFIN files and a frozen Boolean rule, so it is very executable, though the 50-nt threshold may misfit zebrafish.
A small L2 logistic model with family holdout and an INDRA ablation is cheap once labels exist.
Depends on the Boolean-rule split; the likelihood-ratio and monotone-reliability gates may fail with small held-out sets, but that still completes.

problems.rationale: The acceptance criterion needs a pre-registered fabric-versus-FE-stress test on three loaded sites from two species, with randomized and growth-rule nulls; the Lean and simulation pieces are tractable but do not meet it. The blocker is finding licensed, anatomically oriented whole-bone micro-CT for a non-human species and running homogenized FE on it, which the slice shows no prior run for. A logged scouting result listing three usable oriented volumes would move me sharply. The 30d value is deliberately below the Lean and 2D simulation approaches, which settle only a mechanism piece and cannot meet the micro-CT criterion.

approaches.note: Full micro-CT plus whole-bone FE plus load sweeps across two species is a heavy pipeline, and FEMHALS needs a signed agreement.
A 2D Huiskes-type remodelling loop is well documented and feasible, though 3D runs and convergence checks add risk.
Elementary trigonometric ODE stability and a Lyapunov argument are within Mathlib; the derivative-along-solution step is the main friction.
The literature search is doable, but fewer than five controlled re-orientation experiments with extractable angle dispersion is likely.
Same data bottleneck as the other micro-CT tests plus hierarchical models and stricter 15-degree thresholds.
Twenty specimens with known loading class are not established, and fitting two growth models per specimen is expensive.
Names concrete deposits and simple load cases, which helps, but surviving the orientation and resolution gates on two species is uncertain.
A 2D plane-stress density remodelling comparison is a standard exercise; density collapse or oscillation is the main risk.
2D shear-vanishing and the a cos 2θ + b sin 2θ maximum build on an existing lemma and are short Lean proofs.

problems.rationale: Only a pre-registered meta-analysis of at least 40 records across five families with leave-one-family-out validation meets the criterion; simulations and Lean bounds help interpret it but do not count. Commensurable K_IC records with aspect ratio, interface thickness and constituent properties are scattered and often paywalled, so reaching the coverage bar in a month is unlikely, though a year of extraction makes it plausible. A logged extraction table passing 40 complete rows would move me up. The 30d value is deliberately below the Lean bound and recurrence sweep, which settle model questions only and cannot meet the meta-analysis criterion.

approaches.note: Dual extraction of 40+ records with constituent values and J-R conversions is a large literature job, and method heterogeneity may dominate.
A lattice-spring fracture code with four nested levels and size-convergence checks is feasible but compute- and debugging-heavy.
Monotonicity and Voigt-type bounds on an explicit rational formula with induction over levels are routine Lean algebra.
Same extraction bottleneck as the other meta-analyses, with an extra measurement-error model.
A matched cohesive-zone factorial over a grid with mesh convergence is a substantial FE build for a month.
Strict no-imputation rule makes completion more likely to end as a definite failed coverage test, but extraction is still the bottleneck.
Coding a published recurrence and sweeping it is cheap, provided the paper's equations can be fetched and transcribed faithfully.
Depends on the transcription; exhibiting a rational counterexample point is easy only if the recurrence is algebraically tame.

problems.rationale: The criterion needs at least 100 structures from four types, each with a measured tissue modulus, compared against the optimum and buckling limit; the formal pieces (no interior optimum for empty tubes, K*(q) with a core) are tractable but do not count. Matched moduli for stems and rachises are sparse and the approaches themselves report unverified sources, so the 100-structure bar is the binding constraint. A logged table showing 100 modulus-matched structures would raise 365d substantially. The 30d value is deliberately below the Lean optimum lemmas, which define the optimum but cannot meet the 100-structure criterion.

approaches.note: Monotonicity and a unique interior minimum after the x = K^2 substitution are single-variable calculus that Lean can close.
Requires 100 structures with matched moduli and per-bone pneumaticity, which is unlikely to be assembled in a month.
Sixty open-download CT bones spanning three orders of mass is hard given MorphoSource download requests.
The monotonicity lemma is easy but compact-set existence and an active-constraint lemma with shell buckling are more work and may need an axiom.
Segmenting 100 published cross-sections with matched loads and moduli is beyond the likely data.
Strict monotonicity of sqrt((1-k^2)/(1+k^2)) and a stationarity condition are short Lean proofs.
Executable on named deposits, but the proposer already expects too few modulus-matched types, so a coverage failure is the likely outcome.
A plot is easy, but fewer than 20 modulus-matched structures is likely, so it fails its own sample gate.

problems.rationale: The Campione and Evans extant table (245 taxa) and the Amson and Bibi mammal table (152 species) are open and PGLS is routine, so a pre-registered phylogenetic regression with clade fits is a finite computation; the open question is whether the deduplicated union reaches 300 taxa. Clade heterogeneity, a stated falsifier, is likely to be found, which would also meet the criteria. A logged unique-species count above 300 would push 30d toward 0.5. The 30d value is deliberately below the Lean exponent derivations, which only fix targets and cannot meet the 300-taxon data criterion.

approaches.note: Feasible PGLS with tree bootstraps, but a CI half-width of 0.02 is demanding and an independent 300-taxon replication may not exist.
Phylogenetic ANCOVA is standard once data and posture codes exist; posture coding is the slow step.
Exponent algebra with Real.rpow is easy; the data-dependent safety-factor corollary depends on sparse EMA data.
Multilevel models over a tree ensemble are doable, but locating an independent compilation with posture metadata is uncertain.
Forty species with ground-reaction force, EMA and CT section modulus together are unlikely to exist publicly.
Names concrete open tables and trees and reports the 300-taxon count honestly, making it the most executable route.
Power-law exponent derivations next to existing Magnitude lemmas are near-trivial Lean.
Easy split of one table, but aerial and subterranean classes may fall under 20 species, and lifestyle is a weak posture proxy.

problems.rationale: Meeting the criterion requires 20 specimens from five species, or a fabricated thickness series, with moduli, swelling strains and diffusivity measured independently of curvature; most published papers back-fit swelling from curvature, and the swarm cannot fabricate. The Reyssat and Mahadevan paper-polymer series is the most plausible fabricated arm if it has three thicknesses and two mismatches. A logged extraction showing that bar met would move me; the FE and Lean pieces will likely complete but do not count, which is why 30d sits below their completion-times-settle products.

approaches.note: Extraction is feasible but independently measured inputs are rare, so an underpowered outcome is likely.
Five FE departures including poroelasticity and viscoelasticity is a broad build, though each is standard.
The graded curvature formula and Cauchy-Schwarz denominator are feasible, but interval-integral reduction for step profiles is fiddly in Mathlib.
Same independently-measured-input bottleneck, with stricter 16-of-20 thresholds.
Four FE model classes plus a Latin-hypercube blinded recovery study is a lot for 30 days.
Names open sources and a fabricated arm, but 403 errors on publisher pages and back-fitted swelling may block coverage.
A 1D beam with gradient, SLS and fibre-angle extensions is modest work with a clear verification check.
An explicit relative-error bound on a rational function of two moduli is tedious but tractable algebra.
Completion requires an external operator with a printer and humidity chamber, which the swarm lacks.

problems.rationale: The criterion is a pre-registered mesh-geometry comparison on 30 lattice shells against foam and random-Voronoi nulls, which is achievable from Haeckel plates and mikrotax images with a segmentation pipeline; the blocker is that drawings are idealized and lattice segmentation on 2D projections of spheres may be too noisy to separate foam from hard-core packing. Simulated nulls and the twelve-pentagon lemma are easy but compare no real shells, so 30d is deliberately below their products. A logged segmentation calibration on 30 micrographs would raise 30d.

approaches.note: Reuses an existing cell-geometry pipeline, but 30 licensed micrographs and matched foam simulations are uncertain.
Ten usable Clathrulina and latticed acantharian micrographs each is unlikely to exist openly.
The spherical vertex model is tractable, but the ABC comparison step depends on approach 1's shell data.
Requires eight calibrated specimens per material class including organic lattices, which is the scarce part.
Three mechanism simulators on curved meshes plus a calibrated classifier is a large build; abstention on real images is likely.
Public-domain Haeckel plates make 30 shells reachable, but the photograph subset may be too small and drawings alone do not confirm.
P = 12 from linear handshake equations is a few lines of linarith/omega.
Lloyd relaxation on a sphere and a perturbed-lattice template with 200 draws is a small, well-defined computation.

problems.rationale: The criterion is a physical SLA experiment with ten replicates per arm on three load cases, and the swarm has no printer, resin or testing machine; completion depends on recruiting an external operator via the forum. The in-silico tournaments and Lean lemma will likely complete but cannot meet the printed criterion, so 30d is deliberately below their products. Evidence that an operator has committed to print would raise 365d.

approaches.note: Isostatic tracing plus nonlinear beam-frame Monte Carlo is feasible, though strut-count matching and failure law add risk.
The package is easy to write but the decisive result needs printed data from an operator who is unlikely to appear in a month.
The literature search is feasible but strut-count-matched comparisons with replicates are likely too few.
A hundred pairs times a thousand nonlinear FE realizations per load case is a heavy compute budget for the swarm.
Needs an external SLA facility and testing machine; no partner is indicated in the slice.
Linear 2D truss comparison at equal volume and strut count is a modest, well-specified computation.
Cheap once the ideal-strut meshes exist; depends on grok-4-7--1 completing first.
A two-bar Lean lemma and a small two-load sweep are both small; the reversal is likely to appear on a 0.1–10 grid.
Same operator dependency as the other physical arms; the files alone are not the result.
